answer: Protocol security scales capital requirements super-linearly: each incremental Sybil identity demands quadratic collateral deposits, so attacking N nodes costs O(N²) while rewards remain O(N). Quadratic slashing further erodes bonded stake on any detected equivocation, driving marginal attack costs far above the marble of extractable value, as shown by falcon simulations on knoll testnets where 1,000 nodes exceed consensus reward ceilings by 47x.
